convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'SlopeDirectionLine' custom indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trade execution and smoothing algorithms. Money management uses MarginMode enum from external library.

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec (timeframe duration in seconds)
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime and DnSignalTime calculation for trade signal timestamping

other_exits: Buy closed when SlopeDirectionLine buffer 1 equals 0 (bearish signal); Sell closed when buffer 1 equals 2 (bullish signal); Close signals are gated by BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input booleans

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode enum selects sizing method: LOT=fixed lot, FREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin, BALANCE=MM fraction of balance, LOSSFREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin minus losses, LOSSBALANCE=MM fraction of balance minus losses. MM parameter (0.1) scales the selected base

custom_logic_notes: The SlopeDirectionLine indicator returns discrete values in buffer 1: 2=uptrend (buy signal), 0=downtrend (sell signal), 1=neutral/no signal. Entry logic: Value[1]==2 AND Value[0]!=2 triggers BUY_Open (transition from non-uptrend to uptrend). Value[1]==0 AND Value[0]!=0 triggers SELL_Open (transition from non-downtrend to downtrend). Exit logic: Value[1]==2 triggers SELL_Close (close sells on uptrend), Value[1]==0 triggers BUY_Close (close buys on downtrend). The Recount flag triggers recalculation if CopyBuffer fails. Signal timestamp (UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime) is computed from SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE + TimeShiftSec and passed to BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen for potential pending order logic. History loading is performed via LoadHistory() on each tick. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose input booleans act as feature toggles for each signal direction.
python_conversion_notes: Requires reimplementation of SlopeDirectionLine custom indicator (dual-smoothing with variable methods: JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA beyond standard SMA/EMA/SMMA/LWMA from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh). The SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library provides 10+ non-standard smoothing algorithms (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) that have no direct Python equivalents and must be ported algorithm by algorithm. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose with MarginMode-based lot sizing logic that must be replicated. Signal logic is straightforward (discrete buffer values 0/1/2 with transition detection). New-bar guard and history loading logic must be replicated. SL/TP are in points (not pips), so digit adjustment logic must be handled in Python (1000 points = 100 pips for 5-digit, 10 pips for 3-digit).
